body: BusinessDen reported on June 4, 2026 that the owners of 76 Commerce Center, an industrial park in Brighton, Colorado, have sued their tenant, BroadRange Logistics LLC, for $32 million. The plaintiffs, 76 Commerce Center LLC and 76 Commerce Center 3 LLC, are tied to Hyde Development and Mortenson Properties. BroadRange, a Georgia-based third-party logistics company, leased more than 1.1 million square feet at the park in 2024, a deal BusinessDen described as the largest speculative lease in state history.

According to the landlords, BroadRange's tenancy of two buildings at 22250 and 22500 E. I-76 Frontage Road began in September 2024 with six months of free rent. They allege the company began missing its roughly $590,000 monthly rent by August 2025, owed $3.6 million by October 2025, signed an amended lease in November 2025 and kept defaulting until its leases were terminated on March 13, 2026. They seek about $8.9 million in back rent, $17.4 million to recover a discretionary tenant-improvement allowance and $3 million in rent abatement they say became repayable on default, plus interest and late fees.

The Real Deal reported in July that BroadRange faces other landlord suits, including one filed in New York state court by KSG, the owner of a Pennsylvania warehouse, over an $11 million tenant-improvement allowance. The Real Deal said BroadRange has denied the allegations in court filings.
